title: What the venue owner adds to our keyword research

content.job: Standalone list email exploring the central exchange and the roles on each side. Preserve the body exactly. No offer or reply request; send metadata remains proposed.
content.body:
Our team had brought the existing keywords and some proposed additions to the conversation. She explained that the shortened name was familiar to local people, as well as some couples coming from outside the area. If couples use a name like that when they talk about the area, some may use it when they search, and a keyword list put together from outside the market can miss a term like that.

The team agreed to look into her suggestion and share any additional terms they found.

It was a small exchange, but it illustrates something we value in an advertising partnership. Our team contributed the recommendations and the commitment to research. The client contributed context about how people talk about her market.

**Your firsthand knowledge of couples deserves a place alongside our advertising expertise.**

When you're already investing in Google Ads, you want the people supporting you to bring considered recommendations. You also have knowledge gained through the conversations you're having with people who might choose your venue.

Those contributions can work together. The person speaking with couples can offer context that's useful to the team researching how to reach them.

We believe a recommendation should give us something meaningful to discuss with you. There should be room for your experience to contribute while we're considering the strategy, with our team taking responsibility for investigating the questions that arise.

That's what this client brought to the review. She explained a familiar way of referring to the region, and our team gave that suggestion a place in the research conversation.
content.ending:
When a client passes along something from a conversation with couples, we want them to know exactly what our team will do with it next.

Talk soon,
Whitney

content.title: What you hear from couples belongs in your Google Ads strategy.

slides.job: State the promise as an insight about the reader.
slides.text:
What you hear from couples belongs in your Google Ads strategy.

You can hire specialists for their advertising expertise and still bring valuable knowledge to the work. The way couples describe your area is part of what you know from speaking with them, and it deserves room in the research conversation.

slides.job: Establish the prepared recommendations and the invitation.
slides.text:
In a review with a venue client, we brought the current Google keywords and some recommended additions into the discussion.

Then we asked how the list looked to her. That gave her a place to contribute her understanding of the market while the recommendations were still being considered.

slides.job: Keep the client's contribution and conditional reasoning exactly as approved.
slides.text:
She raised the shortened name people use for the region.

She explained that it was familiar to local people and to some couples coming from outside the area. The suggestion came from her knowledge of how people refer to the place where the venue operates. If couples use that name in conversation, some may use it when they search, and a keyword list put together from outside the market can miss it.

slides.job: Resolve the exchange with the evidenced research commitment.
slides.text:
Our answer: we'd look into it and pass along anything else we turned up.

She supplied the local context. We took on the job of investigating it. Her idea joined the recommendations already on the table as one more question for our team to research.

slides.job: Connect the story to an owner who already speaks with couples.
slides.text:
If you run a venue, you're having these conversations, too.

You hear how they describe the location and how familiar it is to them. Those are things you hear firsthand.

slides.job: Explain why an observation need not be a finished advertising recommendation.
slides.text:
What she offered was a possibility for us to examine.

She explained what she knew and why it might be worth a look. Working out whether the shorthand belongs in the campaign is research, and that part stayed with our team.

slides.job: State the partnership belief with a clear division of work.
slides.text:
**We believe your knowledge of couples should shape what we research, while the research itself stays our responsibility.**

You bring context from your market. We investigate what it means for your Google keywords and bring back what we find.

slides.job: Pay off the promise through the team's specific response.
slides.text:
Some owners want a team to manage their ads. Others want us to launch their campaigns, then guide them while they run them.

Either way, what you hear from couples has a place in the work, and we want our keyword conversations to make room for it.

caption.body:
If you already advertise your venue, you've likely brought in help for the parts that take specialist time: the research, the campaign build, the decisions about which searches to pay for. What stays with you is everything you hear from couples.

In one Google keyword review, we brought a venue client the terms already in her account and the additions we were proposing, and asked what she thought. She mentioned the abbreviation people use for her region, and explained that locals use it and so do some couples who come from elsewhere.

We agreed to investigate it and pass along anything else we found. Her part was the context. The research stayed with us.

That's the partnership we want with venue owners: your firsthand view of the market feeding the questions we pursue, and our team doing the work of answering them.
caption.hook: You don't have to know how keyword research works to have something useful to add to it.
caption.ending:
If something a couple says ever makes you wonder about your ads, it's worth bringing into the conversation.

-Whitney

When you already market your venue and speak with the couples considering it, you bring experience that matters to an advertising partnership. Expert support should provide a way for that knowledge to inform the work.

A keyword discussion with a venue client gives a small example. We reviewed the terms already in place and our proposed additions, then invited her perspective. She raised the abbreviation people use for the region and described its familiarity among locals and some couples visiting from elsewhere.

We agreed to investigate and pass along any further terms we found. The client contributed the context; our team committed to the research.

The value of the conversation was in how those contributions met. A prepared recommendation gave us something to discuss, and the client's explanation supplied another possibility to examine.

For someone who already knows the market, specialist support can provide a practical way for that experience to inform what is considered next.

content.title: Regional shorthand in a keyword review
content.script:
A venue client gave our team another phrase to investigate for her Google Ads.

Here's what happened. Our team was reviewing the keywords she already had, along with some additional recommendations. And they asked whether she had any questions or concerns about the list.

She brought up the shorthand people use for her area. She explained that local people use it, and some couples from outside the area do, too. If couples use a name like that when they talk about the area, some of them may use it when they search. A keyword list put together from outside the market can miss a term like that.

Our team said they'd look into it and share any other terms they found.

What stands out to me is how she contributed. She brought something she knew about the way people talk about her market into the research conversation.

When you're speaking with couples, you're hearing language that can be useful to the people working on your ads. We bring our advertising expertise, and you bring that firsthand experience.

I think a good partnership should give both a place in the strategy, so your knowledge of couples can help shape what our team explores.

caption.body:
When you're already investing in Google Ads, you want specialists who can bring a considered recommendation to the table. You also have knowledge of your market that comes from speaking directly with the people choosing a wedding venue.

Those contributions can work together. During a keyword review, our team asked a venue client for questions about the existing terms and the additions being proposed. She suggested looking into a familiar abbreviation for her area, explaining that people used it locally and that it was familiar to some couples travelling in, too. If couples use a name like that in conversation, some may use it when they search.

Our team agreed to research the suggestion and share any further terms they found. Her contribution gave the team another question to pursue.

We believe that kind of exchange belongs in an advertising partnership. The research gives the conversation a starting point, while the client's experience can add something worth exploring. For an owner who already knows the market well, expert support should offer a useful place for that knowledge.
caption.hook: The person talking with your couples has something to add when your Google keywords are reviewed.
caption.ending:
Here, her explanation of a local name was enough to give our team another question to research.

-Whitney

content.title: Starting from the keywords already there
content.script:
What happens to the Google keywords you already have when a specialist team steps in?

With one of our venue clients, ads were already running when our team sat down to review the account. So the review started with the keywords that were already in there.

And the team thought the existing keywords were good. That shaped the whole conversation. The recommended additions came in alongside the current keywords, as a way to build on what was there rather than start over.

There was also a sense of scale. Our team noted that ads were already running when they reviewed the account.

I like that. When you've already put work into your advertising, a good review starts by understanding it, says what's useful about it, and then explains how anything new fits next to it.

caption.body:
When you bring in a specialist team, it's fair to wonder what happens to those choices, and whether anyone will tell you what's worth keeping.

With one of our venue clients, the ads were already live when we reviewed the account. Our team began by making a note of the keywords already in place.

The proposed additions came into the same discussion as ways to build on that list. We want our recommendations to reflect an understanding of the work already in place, so the client can see how the proposed changes relate to what has come before.

For an owner who has invested time in advertising, that changes what a review feels like. You can see the keywords already there and how each proposed addition relates to them.
caption.hook: If you've already been running Google Ads, you've already made choices about which searches matter to your venue.
caption.ending:

content.title: All-inclusive in the keyword proposal

caption.body:
One venue we work with offers all-inclusive weddings, and that offer shaped the Google searches our team proposed.

During a Google keyword review with one of our venue clients, our team pointed to the all-inclusive side of the business as an area of opportunity, because they saw it as something that really sets the venue apart. The proposed keywords included all-inclusive searches for both venues and wedding packages.

The reasoning started with the business itself. This was an option the venue offered, and a couple intentionally searching for it could be looking for that kind of wedding.

Our team also looked at search volume, cost and competition for those terms, brought that context into the conversation, and asked the client how the proposed terms looked to her.

That gives a venue owner more than a list of phrases to approve. You can see why each direction is on the table and what the research says about it.
caption.hook: What your venue offers can point to the Google searches worth looking at.
caption.ending:
Here, the all-inclusive offer gave our team a specific direction to research and explain.

-Whitney
